newsitem.title: USA: Texas spot electricity steady after recent losses.
newsitem.headline: Texas spot electricity steady after recent losses.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) held steady Tuesday against Monday levels after recent losses linked to mild weather and plunging natural gas prices.
The downward price spiral was halted mainly by the lack of players due to the Christmas holiday, market sources said.
"There's just not a lot going on," said a Houston marketer said, adding today's price assessments were mostly notational based on gas prices.
Day-head power values in ERCOT are roughly a third from last week's highs, which were driven by a deep freeze and sky-rocketing gas prices.
Swing gas in south Texas edged down to $3.75 per million British thermal unit (mmBtu) area from Monday's $3.80 in very thin activity.
On the New York Mercantile Exchange, January Henry Hub gas futures, which expire today, were last down 5.2 cents at $4.140, trimming a 20.2 cent loss.
Christmas temperatures in ERCOT were forecast to range in 30-60 Fahrenheit degrees. A revised outlook showed Texas would experience slightly colder-than-normal weather for the rest of the week.
ERCOT firm, peak power for a 16-hour block for Thursday was quoted at $20.00-$25.00 a megawatt hour (MWh), a wider range than Monday's $20.00-$22.00 for Tuesday.
ERCOT firm, peak electricity for Wednesday was valued near $16.00-$17.00.
ERCOT electricity for non-firm delivery during Thursday's heavy load hours was assessed at $19.00-$24.00, compared with Monday's $19.00-$21.00.
Firm off-peak ERCOT deliveries for Thursday remained at $10.00-$14.00.
ERCOT electricity for non-firm delivery during Thursday's light load hours was notationally pegged at $9.00-$13.00.
Balance of December electricity in ERCOT was pegged near $28.00-$29.00. ERCOT January/February prices again talked again near $39.00.
